2020_145_021820spmtg.paragraph: Agenda and supporting packet for a special meeting of the Troy School District Board of Education held at 7:00 PM on February 18, 2020 at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy. The one substantive item was Board Candidate Selection: following the resignation of Mrs. Paula Fleming on January 21, 2020, the Board had to appoint a member to serve through the end of her term, which ends December 31, 2020. The packet holds the nomination and roll-call scripts, an appointment resolution, and written questionnaires from Emina Alic, Vital Anne, Tim Burns, Russell Reynolds, Tony Sarna, Srinivas Simhan, Barrington Wilkins and Lisa Zheng.

**Meeting**
Special meeting of the Troy Board of Education, February 18, 2020, 7:00 PM, Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. Letterhead address 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098; 248.823.4000. The notice states that when school is in session meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m., and can be viewed at http://vimeo.com/troyschools; district site www.troy.k12.mi.us.

**Agenda**
1. Pledge of Allegiance; 2. Public Communication; 3. Board Candidate Selection (packet page 3); 4. Other; 5. Closed Session — Consideration: Negotiations (packet page 54); 6. Adjournment. Items need not be taken in the order shown; consent agenda items are acted on at one time unless removed.

**The vacancy and the process**
Item 3.A, Board Member Nominations and Appointment, recites that due to the resignation of Mrs. Paula Fleming on January 21, 2020 the Board must appoint an individual to serve through the end of Mrs. Fleming's term of office, ending December 31, 2020. The Board president accepts nominations from Board members, and individual Board members may not nominate more than one candidate. Blank nomination lines are provided for a first, second and third nominee; the president then asks for further nominations, pauses, and closes nominations. Roll-call sheets with YES and NO lines follow for each nominee, with the member order rotating across Hammond, Hauff, Philippart, Schmidt, Wilson and Gottlieb. A suggested resolution with Moved by / Supported by lines reads: "Be It Therefore Resolved that ____ be appointed to fill the vacancy on the Board of Education for the term expiring December 31, 2020," voted by roll call beginning with Schmidt. No results, nominators or appointee are recorded in the document.

**Candidate materials**

| Candidate | Packet page | Snapshot from the questionnaire |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Emina Alic | 6 | Divider page only; no extracted text in the source |
| Vital Anne | 12 | Vice-President of Software Integrity and Testing at Altair; in Troy 16 years |
| Tim Burns | 21 | Criminal defense attorney; Oakland County Commissioner 2007-2011 |
| Russell Reynolds | 26 | Billing and accounting analyst at Shift Digital, Birmingham |
| Tony Sarna | 32 | Troy High graduate; co-owner of three technology businesses |
| Srinivas Simhan | 39 | Software developer at Blue Cross Blue Shield; FRC Team 226 mentor |
| Barrington Wilkins | 43 | Attorney, U.S. Attorney's Office in Detroit |
| Lisa Zheng | 47 | Stanford MS EE and Wharton MBA; investment and consulting background |

The questionnaire asks fourteen numbered questions covering biography, engagement in Troy outside the district, relationship to the district, advocacy for children, lobbying experience, motivation, perceived strengths and challenges, willingness to defend the seat in the November 2020 election, unique skills, the role of a trustee, expected challenges as a newcomer, professional development and travel (MASB, NSBA, the NSBA Federal Advocacy Conference in Washington D.C., National Equity Project, Deeper Learning Conference), and any closing remarks.

**Closed session**
Item 5.A directs that the Board pass a resolution to go into closed session to discuss negotiations, after which no additional business will take place other than to officially adjourn. The resolution cites the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8 (c), with a roll call listing Wilson, Gottlieb, Hammond, Hauff, Philippart and Schmidt.

**Item 3.A — Board Member Nominations and Appointment.** Due to the resignation of Mrs. Paula Fleming on January 21, 2020, the Board is required to appoint an individual to serve through the end of Mrs. Fleming's term of office, which ends on December 31, 2020. The Board president will accept nominations from Board members, and individual Board members may not nominate more than one candidate. The script prints the formula "I, ____, nominate ____ to fill the vacancy on the Board of Education for the term ending December 31, 2020" three times, then closes nominations. Roll-call sheets with YES and NO lines follow for a First, Second and Third Nominee (if necessary), rotating the order across Hammond, Hauff, Philippart, Schmidt, Wilson and Gottlieb. No nominators, votes or appointee are recorded.

**Candidate questionnaires.** Each applicant answered the "2020 Troy School Board Appointed Trustee Candidate Questionnaire," a fourteen-question instrument on biography, community and district involvement, advocacy, lobbying, strengths and challenges, readiness to defend the seat in the November 2020 election, and willingness to travel to Michigan Association of School Boards (MASB) and National School Board Association events, the NSBA Federal Advocacy Conference in Washington D.C., the National Equity Project and the Deeper Learning Conference, for which TSD covers direct expenses but does not reimburse missed work.

*Emina Alic* — the divider page is present but her application pages carry no extracted text in this source.

*Vital Anne* — Vital L. Anne, age 49, married 26 years to Siva, in Troy 16 years, daughters aged 20 and 16. BE in Mechanical Engineering from Andhra University in India (1991) and an MS in Biomechanics from Purdue University in Indianapolis; 25 years at Altair in Troy, now Vice-President of Software Integrity and Testing; a citizen since 2006. Her daughters attended Niles preschool, Morse Elementary, Baker Middle School and International Academy East, and Hill Elementary, Larson Middle School and Athens High School. Involvement: Troy Parks and Recreation volleyball, Bharatiya Temple, Troy Telugu Association, MDOT Adopt-a-Highway cleanup on I-75 between Coolidge and Square Lake (2013-2018), Troy Citizens Academy, poll work, Morse PTO (2007-2009), Baker Science Olympiad with Mrs. Herberholz (state qualification in 2013, 2nd and 5th place medals), Larson Science Olympiad with Mrs. Sandra Bammel (2015-2017), IAE PTO and IAE Music Parents Association (2014-2017), Athens Athletic Boosters and Athens PTO (2018-current), regional HOSA (2019), and Detroit Education Society tutoring. She recounts the 2009/2010 Troy Public Library millage campaign and a 2013-2014 IAEMPA effort in which four senior parents met then-superintendent Dr. Barbara Fowler after orchestra teacher Mrs. Mayes reported an unheated annex music room. She calls Troy the fourth largest city in Michigan by property value, cites 35 to 40% foreign-born households and 83 languages, states K-12 funding declined by 30 percent between 2002 and 2017 after inflation and that Michigan ranks dead last (50th) in education revenue growth.

*Tim Burns* — married fifteen years to Barbra, father of eleven-year-old twins Jackson and Margaret, both in 5th Grade at Costello Elementary School. Raised in St. Clair, Michigan; a Page in the U.S. House of Representatives; Bradley University; law school at University of Detroit/Mercy; admitted to the Michigan Bar in 2000; twelve years in his own criminal defense practice; a recent term on the Board of Commissioners for the State Bar of Michigan. Service includes the Troy Jaycees, the Oakland County Board of Commissioners from 2007-2011, the Troy Community Coalition for the Prevention of Drug & Alcohol Abuse board including a year as President, "Citizen of the Year" from the Troy Elks Lodge in 2011, the Clawson-Troy Optimist Club and the Troy Historical Society. The family moved into the district in July 2019 after five years in the Royal Oak School District; he has been a mock-trial attorney at the Oakland County Circuit Court's Constitution Day event for five years. He cites food-allergy advocacy recognized by F.A.R.E. (Food Allergy Research & Education), the Oakland County Bar Association Legislative Committee, a son with ADHD and a daughter with Dyslexia, and, as an Oakland County Parks Commissioner, a reversal that doubled the size of Independence Oaks. He names enrollment versus capacity as a leading challenge and gives his cell as 248-225-1497.

*Russell Reynolds* — raised in Green Bay, Wisconsin, graduating in 2007; Associate's Degree in Accounting from Northeast Wisconsin Technical College (2009) and president of his Phi Theta Kappa chapter; Bachelor's in Accounting (2011) and a second Bachelor's in Business with an Economics minor (2013) from Lakeland College. He is a billing and accounting analyst at Shift Digital in Birmingham, where he has worked almost 5 years. He and his wife Emily bought a 1925 craftsman-style farmhouse in 2014; Emily has taught science at International Academy East for 5 years after 6 years at Romeo High School. He taught two Personal Finance enrichment courses at IAE and coached youth soccer for 5 years including the Denmark High School girls team. He has met with State Representative Padma Kuppa and names the proposed merger with the Clawson School District, teacher burnout and funding uncertainty as coming obstacles, noting he is relatively new to the Troy area (6 years).

*Tony Sarna* — Louis Anthony Sarna IV, who attended Leonard Elementary School for kindergarten, Hamilton Elementary School for first through fifth grades, Smith Middle School and Troy High School, and took architecture courses at Lawrence Technological University. In 2000 he and a partner took their Web development company, HyperTK Corporation, full time; he graduated magna cum laude from Baker College in Auburn Hills with a Bachelor of Computer Information Systems, was named Baker College's Outstanding Graduate, and served eight years on its Academic Advisory Board. He co-founded the email marketing service Savvy Sender in 2012 and acquired Link Sky Value Host in 2015. He is a graduate of the City of Troy's Citizens' Academy XIV. He lives in Troy with his wife Melissa and their boys Anthony (8), Lucas (6) and Lincoln (almost 4); Anthony and Lucas attend Leonard and Lincoln the new Troy School District Preschool. In 2017 his family was featured in Firefighters Park Living magazine, since rebranded North Troy Living. He leads a first grade Tiger den and a third grade Bear den, sits on the Delzair Homeowners' Association board and is active in the Leonard PTO. His resume includes a reference from Ethan Baker, Mayor of the City of Troy, plus letters from Erin L. Detmer, Ph.D., Principal of Leonard Elementary School; Tracy Gonzalez, Cub Scout Pack 1703 Cubmaster; and Ryan R. Koerber.

*Srinivas Simhan* — born in Texas, attended Schroeder Elementary, Hamilton Elementary, Boulan Park Middle School and Troy High School ('14), and graduated from the University of Michigan-Dearborn ('19) in Computer Science. He is a software developer at Blue Cross Blue Shield in Detroit and works with STEM programs such as The Robot Garage. He mentors FIRST FRC Team 226 Hammerheads, comprising over 100+ students from Troy High School, Athens High School and International Academy East, and Troy Youth Robotics, which has helped form over 60+ teams. He has volunteered or competed at over 85 events, co-hosting 15 in Troy. Since 2017 he has taken part in The Michigan Advocacy Conference (MAC), connecting with Senator McMorrow, State Representative Padma Kuppa and Senator Peters, and cites relationships with General Motors, Ford, Denso and Siemens. He names space and resource allocation and after-school program funding as the largest challenges.

*Barrington Wilkins* — originally from Washington, D.C.; he and his wife moved to the Troy area 11 years ago with two children and have since added two more. He graduated from the University of Maryland, attended Brigham Young University for law school, and is an attorney with the U.S. Attorney's Office in Detroit. He coaches a fifth grade basketball team of Martell and Leonard students; two of his children attend Martell and one Smith Middle School. He has worked with DOJ's Project Sentry, the Explorer Scout program, TutorMate, and the Detroit Summer Legal Institute sponsored by the University of Detroit's Mercy School of Law. He names the district's resources as its greatest strength and "functional diversity" as its greatest challenge.

*Lisa Zheng* — listed as ZHENG, YIN LISA, USA citizenship, lisayzh@gmail.com, mobile +1-248-321-4415. She attended GMI (now Kettering University, Flint, MI) on scholarship in Electrical Engineering while co-oping at Rockwell International Automotive in Troy, earned a Master's in EE at Stanford University with a full tuition waiver and stipend, worked on satellite communication payloads in Silicon Valley, then earned an MBA in Finance at the Wharton School, University of Pennsylvania, and worked in investment banking in Manhattan on corporate restructuring, debt issuance, mergers and acquisitions and business valuation. Earlier work included the Army Research Lab in Illinois, AT&T in New Jersey and DSC Communications in California. After the 9/11 attack she moved to Taiwan, living there primarily for the past 15 years; the family returned in the summer of 2019. Her parents have lived in Troy and the surrounding vicinity since 1991; her twins are 7th graders at Boulan Park Middle School. Since enrolling them at BPMS in September 2019 she completed the Troy Citizens Academy, joined HealthyTroy and took part in MLK Service day at Athens HS. Listed roles: Stanford University Undergraduate Admission interview officer (FY2019-current), University of Pennsylvania MBA Admission interviewer (2014-2016), and volunteering at an overseas public elementary school and after-school American School program (2013-2019). She names strategic resource deployment as the district's greatest challenge.

**Item 5.A — Closed Session, Consideration: Negotiations.** The Board must pass a resolution to go into closed session to discuss negotiations, after which no additional business will take place other than to officially adjourn the meeting. The recommended action is to adopt a resolution reading that, as permitted in the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8 (c), the Troy Board of Education shall go into closed session to discuss negotiations, with Moved by and Supported by lines and a roll call listing Wilson, Gottlieb, Hammond, Hauff, Philippart and Schmidt.
